routes.label: Fill the angles around a vertex

question:
A regular polygon of \(m\) sides is exactly enclosed (no overlaps, no gaps) by \(m\) regular polygons of \(n\) sides each. (Shown here for \(m=4,\) \(n=8.\)) If \(m=10,\) what is the value of \(n?\)

[Figure 1](figures/1994_AMC_12_Q26_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The useful place to look is a vertex of the enclosed polygon. In the enclosure shown, one surrounding polygon shares each central side, so the central polygon and its two neighboring polygons fill the angles around that vertex.

[Figure 1](figures/1994_AMC_12_Q26_question_fig1.svg)

A regular decagon has interior angle
\[
\frac{(10-2)180^\circ}{10}=144^\circ.
\]
Let \(x\) be the interior angle of each surrounding regular polygon. Because there are no overlaps or gaps,
\[
144^\circ+2x=360^\circ,
\qquad x=108^\circ.
\]
For a regular \(n\)-gon, where \(n\geq3\), the interior angle is \(180^\circ-360^\circ/n\). Thus
\[
180^\circ-\frac{360^\circ}{n}=108^\circ,
\qquad \frac{360^\circ}{n}=72^\circ,
\qquad n=5.
\]
Therefore the answer is \(\boxed{5}\), choice A.
